messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=redwood-hosted-api, trigger=inference-queue-exhausted, severity=high. Incident URL: https://pagerduty.example/INC123456 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Paging primary oncall @emma (oncall). Policy: primary->secondary->manager. Attempt 1 sent to phone.
pagerduty: No ACK from @emma after 3m — auto-escalation firing to secondary @maya.
maya (secondary): ack  — I'm awake and checking logs now :eyes:
emma (oncall): just saw the push notification, was on DND in a train tunnel, sorry. i'm awake now but if @maya has it, hand off to her.
maya (secondary): thanks. first glance: backend inference queue length spiked on region-us-east-1, worker pods scaling up but token-throttles triggered. seeing 502s at the gateway.
ryan (infra): looking at infra metrics, GPU worker pool cpu/mem fine, but redis (kv-cache) connection errors around the same time.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook suggestion: "inference-queue-exhausted" -> immediate steps: 1) toggle emergency-rate-limit for noisy keys, 2) failover traffic to dedicated-pool, 3) increase kv-cache replicas. Link: https://runbooks.internal/inference/queue-exhausted
sanjay: can someone paste the relevant logs? need to assess customer impact and whether to open P1 bridge.
maya (secondary): pasting logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-14T02:11:03Z] inference-gateway ERROR request_id=abc123 status=502 upstream_error=kv_cache_conn_reset
[2026-03-14T02:11:08Z] worker-1 WARN queue_len=1245 kv_cache_miss_rate=0.98 model=gpt-infer-13b
[2026-03-14T02:11:09Z] autoscaler INFO scale_event target=+4pods reason=queue_spike
```
maya (secondary): kv_cache_miss_rate was >0.9 for 45s. looks like cache backend hitting a connection storm.
ryan (infra): confirmed: redis primary reported fd exhaustion at 02:10:57Z, hitting file descriptor limit after a follow-JVM-client reconnect storm from a recent rollout.
liam (manager): paging in parallel — can we mitigate customer impact quickly? if this is cache backend, fail traffic to dedicated pool and reduce load.
maya (secondary): initiating temporary failover to dedicated pool for the affected route. command run: ```redwood-cli route failover --route "api://v1/generate" --to-pool dedicated-us-east-1-A --reason "kv-cache outage"```
incident-bot: Action recorded: route failover requested by @maya.
maya (secondary): also applying emergency rate-limit on public API key xyz: ```curl -X POST https://console.internal/configs/rate-limit -d '{"key":"xyz","limit":20}'``` — reduces bursty tenants.
pagerduty: Manager escalation attempt to @liam sent (because primary didn't ack within policy window).
liam (manager): on call if needed, joining. what customer(s) impacted?
customer-success: saw an alert from one key customer (RealtimeChatCo) reporting timeouts. ticket #CS-987 attached. they saw 502s and increased latencies.
sanjay: taking customer impact: approx 4% of total requests in us-east had 5-15s tail latencies, ~0.7% 502 errors. no data loss reported. SLO blip probable, recommend P1 bridge for triage/mitigation and postmortem.
maya (secondary): failover completed, traffic drain started. new metrics: gateway 502s dropping to near 0 within 90s.
ryan (infra): increasing redis fd limit & restarting replica set to clear connections. commands: ```kubectl -n infra set env redis-statefulset REDIS_MAX_FDS=65536 && kubectl rollout restart sts/redis-statefulset -n infra```
maya (secondary): verifying worker health: `redwood-cli health checks --filter inference --region us-east` => workers back to normal, KV miss rate dropping to 0.12.
emma (oncall): thanks for taking lead @maya, I'm available to hand back if you want.
liam (manager): good triage. @maya @ryan can you add temporary mitigation notes to the incident doc and include exact timestamps for failover and rate-limit so CS can patch customers?
maya (secondary): will add: failover started 3950123360, rate-limit applied 3950123385, redis restart completed 3950123430.
sanjay: summary for post-incident: root cause = redis fd exhaustion after client reconnect storm post-rollout. contributing = insufficient fd limits + noisy tenant. mitigations = emergency rate-limit, failover to dedicated pool, redis replica restart, increase FD limit. action items: 1) permanent fd limit bump, 2) add connection backoff in client, 3) add detection/auto-failover for cache backend.
customer-success: informed RealtimeChatCo and offered temporary credits; they acknowledged and will monitor traffic.
liam (manager): thanks team. I'll set a follow-up meeting tomorrow for the postmortem. if no further issues in next 2 hours we can close the PD incident and update severity to minor. :thumbsup:
pagerduty: Incident INC123456 auto-updated: status=acknowledged, escalation=complete.
incident-bot: Incident thread closed for active mitigation; follow-up tasks assigned in Jira: RD-1472, RD-1473.
maya (secondary): leaving detailed notes in the incident doc now — ping me if you need any extra logs.
emma (oncall): thanks everyone — good handoff.
customer-success: customer confirms trend returning to normal, marking as monitoring. :white_check_mark:
